Bug_Details:
The Comparable.compareTo method returns a negative integer, zero, or a positive integer to indicate whether the object is less than,
equal to, or greater than the parameter. The sign of the return value or whether it is zero is what matters, not its magnitude.
Returning a positive or negative constant value other than the basic ones (-1, 0, or 1) provides no additional information to the caller. Moreover,
it could potentially confuse code readers who are trying to understand its purpose.
Bug_Explanation: The Comparable.compareTo method is supposed to return a negative integer, zero, or a positive integer to indicate whether the object is less than, equal to, or greater than the parameter. However, the code returns Integer.MIN_VALUE which is a negative value and is not a valid return value for compareTo method. This will result in inconsistencies and unexpected behaviors when sorting or comparing objects.
Trigger_Explanation: This test is designed to trigger the bug in the compareTo method of BuggyComparable class. The bug itself is that compareTo method should not return Integer.MIN_VALUE. If it does, this test will fail because it expects to catch an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, which will be thrown when sorting the buggyList in showBug method.
